chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

There is no visiting the sick for eye ailments, and a sick-visit does not take place within less than three days. When it becomes necessary, then one day yes and one day no. When the illness is prolonged, the sick person and his family are left (to manage on their own).

key_terms.عِيَادَة: sick-visiting; the Islamic practice and communal obligation of visiting those who are ill
key_terms.عِيَال: family dependants; those financially and socially dependent on the patient
key_terms.وَجَع الْعَيْن: eye ailment/sore eyes; excluded from the standard rules of عيادة because it requires rest and limited visitors

ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic rules for visiting the sick according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes three distinct rules for visiting the sick (عيادة): eye conditions are excluded from the duty of sick-visiting; formal visitation only begins after three days of illness; once warranted, visits should alternate every other day; and when illness becomes chronic, the obligation lapses and the patient's household takes over care. This teaching reflects early Islamic medical etiquette and social welfare norms, ensuring that obligatory communal duties like sick-visiting remain proportionate and practical.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There is no visiting regarding the eye sores, and a visitation does not happen to be in less than three days. So when it necessitates, so one day, and one day not (every other day). So when the illness gets prolonged, leave the patient and his family (to look after him)’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from certain persons of his people who have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

visit is not necessary for one’s illness of eyes, also not before every three days, unless needed in which case it should take place with a one-day interval in between. If an illness prolongs, then the patient is left in the care of his family.”
